framework: CEFR Companion Volume; IELTS official test format and public assessment criteria
principles: Learning outcomes are written as observable can-do tasks.
Each course develops listening, reading, spoken interaction, spoken production, and writing.
Grammar and vocabulary are taught as tools for completing real communication tasks.
A learner target is a goal, not an official CEFR certificate or IELTS score prediction.

cefr_route.exit: Handle familiar everyday exchanges: introduce yourself, ask and answer simple questions, describe routine and familiar places, give basic past and future information. Pass the A1 skill check in all four skills and complete a teacher-reviewed speaking task.
Understand frequently used expressions; communicate in routine tasks; describe background and immediate needs; complete an integrated four-skill check.
syllabus: Integrated everyday tasks and A2 checkpoint

cefr_route.exit: Understand the main points of clear standard input, manage familiar situations, produce connected text, and explain plans and opinions with reasons.
syllabus: Integrated B1 project and four-skill check

cefr_route.exit: Interact with greater fluency, understand more complex texts, and write clear, developed responses across familiar and academic topics.
syllabus: Integrated B2 project and four-skill check

cefr_route.exit: Use English flexibly and effectively for academic, professional, and social purposes; complete a calibrated four-skill assessment.
syllabus: Integrated C1 portfolio and four-skill check

cefr_route.exit: Understand virtually everything heard or read and communicate precisely, fluently, and flexibly across complex contexts.
syllabus: Integrated C2 capstone and calibrated assessment

ielts_route.entry: Complete A1 and A2, then pass a teacher-reviewed B1 readiness check. Build broad language ability before intensive exam practice; no CEFR level is presented as a guaranteed IELTS band.
ielts_route.choice: At IELTS entry, learner chooses Academic or General Training according to their institution, work, or migration requirement. Listening and Speaking preparation is shared; Reading and Writing preparation follows the chosen test type.

stages.name: IELTS Foundation
stages.focus: diagnostic across four skills; core vocabulary and grammar gaps; listening for gist and detail; reading strategies; paragraph structure; speaking fluency and pronunciation

stages.name: IELTS Skills
stages.focus: official task types; timing; note completion and matching; reading question strategies; Writing Task 1 and Task 2; Speaking Parts 1–3; feedback using public criteria

stages.name: IELTS Practice
stages.focus: timed section practice; full-length mock tests; error logs; targeted revision; teacher-reviewed speaking and writing

twelve_week_plan: 2 · Listening: form, note, and table completion
3 · Listening: matching, map, and multiple choice
4 · Reading: skimming, scanning, and locating evidence
5 · Reading: matching headings, True/False/Not Given, and paraphrase
6 · Writing Task 1: Academic visual report OR General Training letter
7 · Writing Task 2: position, paragraphing, support, and cohesion
8 · Speaking Part 1: familiar topics, fluency, and clear answers
9 · Speaking Part 2: cue-card planning and a sustained talk
10 · Speaking Part 3: developing, comparing, and supporting opinions
11 · Timed four-skill mock sections and diagnostic error log
12 · Targeted remediation, second mock, and readiness review
ielts_route.academic_writing: Task 1 describes visual information; Task 2 responds to a point of view, argument, or problem.
ielts_route.general_writing: Task 1 is a letter; Task 2 responds to a point of view, argument, or problem.
ielts_route.score_policy: Show practice performance and rubric evidence separately from official IELTS results. Only an official IELTS test can award an official band score.

assessment.mastery: Passing a quiz alone is not the unit exit: require a real communication task and teacher feedback. Revisit missed language after spaced intervals using changed contexts.
assessment.question_reuse: Avoid the same question in consecutive attempts. Recycle the same learning objective later with a new prompt because retrieval and review support retention.

weekly_rhythm: Day 1–4: one lesson per day, with a short retrieval review from earlier lessons.
Day 5: 20-item mixed checkpoint, unit mission, and teacher feedback.
At approximately 1, 3, and 7 days after learning: brief spaced vocabulary/grammar retrieval in a new context.
quality_gates: Every lesson has an approved can-do outcome, source-page map, answer key, transcript or model, and accessible Uzbek instructions.

A lead English teacher with advanced proficiency and documented ELT experience authors lessons; a second teacher reviews accuracy, level appropriateness, and answer keys. IELTS reviewers must be trained to use the relevant public band descriptors.
Share scanned textbook pages with enrolled learners only when the course has the necessary distribution permission; otherwise replace them with original page-linked explanations and exercises.
IELTS exercises use official public formats and rubrics; tasks are not labelled as official IELTS questions unless licensed and sourced as such.
Pilot with a small learner group; measure lesson completion, missed objectives, confusing instructions, teacher response time, and bot delivery errors before broad release.
AI may explain and suggest practice but must not certify a CEFR level, predict an official IELTS score, unlock a course, or alter system settings.
